clips.title: IVR presses 1 then 2
clips.blurb: Two digits the way a menu collects an order-status choice.

clips.title: Ringback teaching tone
clips.blurb: 440 Hz and 480 Hz, the classic North American ringback pair, as a short example.

clips.title: Busy cadence
clips.blurb: Two short bursts. Campaign fast-busy is a quota symptom, not this tone alone.

clips.title: Recording beep
clips.blurb: A 1400 Hz beep you can put in mind next to the recording prompt.

clips.title: Agent join
clips.blurb: A two-note chime for the moment whisper ends and the agent is connected.

clips.title: Error branch
clips.blurb: A falling pair. Use it when you demonstrate an unconnected error port.

clips.title: Out of hours
clips.blurb: Three descending notes for the out-of-hours branch.

clips.title: Callback accepted
clips.blurb: A rising pair for a callback offer the caller accepted.

clips.title: Queue tick
clips.blurb: A soft tick each time a waiting contact ages in a demo.

clips.title: Whisper sting
clips.blurb: A short sting for the agent whisper, before the customer is joined.

clips.title: Disconnect
clips.blurb: A single low tone for the disconnect block.

clips.title: 933-style double beep
clips.blurb: Two beeps standing in for a test readback. This is not a recording of a live test call.

clips.title: Hold motif
clips.blurb: Four quiet notes. A real hold flow should use a prompt you own.
